newsitem.title: USA: D'Amato says Swiss will not administer Holocaust fund.
newsitem.headline: D'Amato says Swiss will not administer Holocaust fund.

text.p: The U.S. Senate's sternest critic of Switzerland said on Thursday the Swiss government had assured him it would not decide who receives money from a $100 million fund for Holocaust victims now being established.

Senate Banking Committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato, who blasted Switzerland only a day ago for attempting to manage the fund, told a New York state assembly hearing that Swiss officials assured him the government would "only be a temporary repository" for the money being collected.

He said he had met privately in the morning with Swiss officials who assured him that discussions were under way with Jewish groups to determine how the fund should be administered and added, "I feel much better about that."
Swiss Consul General Alfred Defago, one of the officials who met with D'Amato, told the committee the fund now topped $100 million after a donation by Swiss businesses.
He added that the government would soon decide how much it would contribute and legislation was being prepared to allow the Swiss central bank to make a donation.

"The fund's principal purpose is to distribute money without delay to needy Holocaust survivors," Defago said, adding that the secretary general of the World Jewish Congress, Israel Singer, had been invited to fly to Switzerland for talks with Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti on the issue next week.

Both D'Amato and the WJC have pressed for months for the creation of a Holocaust memorial fund as a good faith gesture by the Swiss government after embarrassing revelations about the role of neutral Switzerland during the war.

D'Amato said that "thousands upon thousands of people are out there with bona fide claims" for compensation from Swiss banks, which have been accused of holding onto unclaimed bank accounts of Holocaust victims.
The assembly's banking committee held the hearing to determine if legislation was needed to force the Swiss to return unclaimed assets.

New York State Comptroller Carl McCall, who two weeks ago stopped overnight deposits of state funds in Swiss banks, told the committee he was now reconsidering that action and could lift the ban on Friday after a meeting of Jewish groups with Swiss officials.
